name: realized-vol-scaled-exposure-1m-recalibrated
rationale: 2026-10-19 lead #3 (repeated as 2026-10-25 lead #4): `realized-vol-scaled-exposure` was calibrated for 1h bars (24-bar window, REFERENCE_HOURLY_VOL 0.0042), so on 1-minute bars its factor sat at the 1.5 cap on 100% of bars and the test was not a fair test of volatility scaling. This re-runs the same inverse-variance damping recalibrated for 1-minute bars: a 1,440-bar (24h) window and a reference of 0.0005, the mean rolling-1440 population stdev of 1-minute simple returns measured on the pre-holdout training window 2026-09-27T17:09Z..2026-10-14T19:00Z (median 0.000515, p10 0.000361, p90 0.000612; close to the 0.0042/sqrt(60) = 0.00054 rescale). With clamp [0.5, 1.5], the p90 bar gets k ~0.67 and the p10 bar hits the 1.5 cap, so the factor actually varies. Practitioner evidence (Man Group, see paper_reference) reports volatility scaling of BTC exposure improving Sharpe by ~0.4 and reducing tail risk. Config is experiments/baseline-config.json unchanged.
code_change_summary: Two parts. (1) Additive: add a `realized_vol: Option<f64>` field to IndicatorPoint (src/signal/mod.rs) and populate it in compute_indicators() as the population standard deviation of the last REALIZED_VOL_WINDOW = 1440 close-to-close simple returns (i.e. over the trailing 1,440 candles = 24h at the pipeline's 1-minute resolution, matching live BASE_RESOLUTION = 60), None until at least REALIZED_VOL_WINDOW+1 closes have been seen. Compute it from the candle close series compute_indicators already iterates, keeping a small rolling buffer of the previous closes; do not add a new indicator struct under src/signal/indicators/ unless that is genuinely cleaner on dev's current structure. Every other IndicatorPoint field and all existing indicator code MUST stay byte-for-byte identical, and any struct-literal construction sites of IndicatorPoint elsewhere in the tree (including tests and src/backtest/) must be updated to set the new field. (2) In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), after ta_normalized is computed and before it is blended with sentiment, damp its deviation from neutral by a volatility factor: let k = ((REFERENCE_MINUTE_VOL / realized_vol).powi(2)).clamp(VOL_SCALE_MIN, VOL_SCALE_MAX) with REFERENCE_MINUTE_VOL = 0.0005 (the mean rolling-1440 1-minute return stdev measured on the pre-holdout training window 2026-09-27..2026-10-14), VOL_SCALE_MIN = 0.5 and VOL_SCALE_MAX = 1.5, all three as named private constants with a comment giving the formula, its inputs and its expected range; then ta_normalized = 0.5 + (ta_normalized - 0.5) * k. The inverse-*variance* (.powi(2)) form is deliberate: it is what Moreira & Muir scale portfolio weight by. When raw.realized_vol is None (warmup) or is not strictly positive and finite, k MUST be 1.0 so the function reduces exactly to today's behaviour -- guard explicitly rather than relying on clamp, since f64::clamp propagates NaN instead of clamping it (the same hazard the 2026-09-08 damped-crossover diff had to guard). The blend with sentiment, the [0.0,1.0] clamp on the result, and the empty-sub_signals warmup guard returning None all stay exactly as they are. Keep the rolling buffer O(1) per candle (running sum and sum of squares, or an equivalent incremental update) since the window is now 1,440 bars, and if the live SignalEngine path cannot provide 1,440 closes, realized_vol must be None there so live behaviour falls back to k = 1.0 (report this as a suspected live/backtest gap rather than silently working around it). TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT and REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT stay at dev's current values (0.25 / 1.0).
constraints: This hypothesis modifies the body of TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. This change MUST be made only on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch -- never as a direct commit to dev/main.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) -- only its body.
MUST NOT change any individual sub-signal's own formula, nor the zone boundaries or apply_zone; only the post-aggregation damping of ta_normalized and the new IndicatorPoint field are added.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the compute_btc_target_* unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs -- update their expected values if the new formula legitimately changes them (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass). Points with realized_vol = None must be unaffected by construction; verify that rather than assume it. Add unit tests covering: k = 1.0 exactly at REFERENCE_MINUTE_VOL, damping toward neutral at high volatility, amplification capped at VOL_SCALE_MAX at low volatility, and a None/zero/NaN realized_vol reducing to today's output.

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body, so the reviewer gives it the scrutiny an allocation-formula change deserves.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or anything on the live order-submission path.

paper_reference.title: Crypto: Too Hot to Handle?
paper_reference.key_claim: Sizing a bitcoin position inversely to ex-ante volatility (30% target) improved its Sharpe by ~0.4 versus unscaled exposure over 2012-2024 and reduced volatility-of-volatility and left-tail expected shortfall, across several estimator half-lives.
paper_reference.pros: Same asset; the inverse-volatility sizing rule maps directly onto damping shirube's allocation deviation by realized vol, and the claim was robust across estimator responsiveness.
paper_reference.cons: Daily data on a long-only position, not 1-minute allocation timing on bitFlyer BTC/JPY; no transaction costs modeled; practitioner piece without an out-of-sample protocol.
